discovery: Prediction and discovery of baryon acoustic oscillations as a cosmic standard ruler

nominees.name: Rashid Sunyaev
nominees.affiliation: Max Planck Institute for Astrophysics, Garching

nominees.name: Daniel Eisenstein
nominees.affiliation: Harvard University (Center for Astrophysics | Harvard & Smithsonian)

motivation: Sound waves in the primordial photon-baryon plasma froze into the matter distribution at recombination, leaving a characteristic scale of about 150 Mpc. Sunyaev (with Zeldovich) predicted this imprint in 1970. In 2005 Eisenstein, leading the SDSS analysis, and Cole, leading the 2dFGRS analysis, independently detected the acoustic peak in galaxy clustering. This gave cosmology a standard ruler calibrated by well-understood linear physics, largely free of the astrophysical systematics such as dust and progenitor evolution that affect standard candles. Baryon acoustic oscillations independently confirmed the accelerating expansion, tied the late universe to the CMB, and are now the basis of BOSS, eBOSS, DESI and Euclid. The 2024–2025 DESI results, which hint at evolving dark energy, show that the method can probe fundamental physics. Together these contributions changed how we measure the cosmos.
